person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: single-cell RNA-seq expression, in which a gene is either strongly positive or undetected, and the reason for the zero cannot be read off the zero
span.quote: First, single-cell expression has repeatedly been shown to exhibit a characteristic bimodal expression pattern, wherein the expression of otherwise abundant genes is either strongly positive or undetected within individual cells.

span.label: how to test for differential expression when the detection rate itself carries both technical and biological variation
span.quote: We and other groups [ 4 – 7 ] have shown that the proportion of cells with detectable expression reflects both technical factors and biological differences between samples.

span.label: a two-part generalized linear model that parameterises the discrete and the continuous halves of bimodal expression, with the cellular detection rate adjusted for as a covariate
span.quote: We propose a two-part, generalized linear model for such bimodal data that parameterizes both of these features.

span.label: method
span.quote: We propose a two-part, generalized linear model for such bimodal data that parameterizes both of these features.

span.label: bimodal single-cell expression, where the technical dropout and the biological extrinsic noise arrive in the same measurement
span.quote: This is due in part to low starting quantities of RNA such that many genes will be below the threshold of detection, but there is also a biological component to this variation (termed extrinsic noise in the literature) that is conflated with the technical variability

span.label: a hurdle model fitted per gene, with the cellular detection rate as a covariate, validated against simulated confounding and applied to MAIT cell activation data
span.term: a hurdle model fitted per gene, with the cellular detection rate as a covariate, validated against simulated confounding and applied to MAIT cell activation data
span.quote: We explored the effect of confounding between the CDR and treatment effects on the MAST false positive rate in the presence and absence of CDR control in the MAST model (Additional file 1 : Figure S4A, B). Controlling for CDR improved the sensitivity and specificity of MAST in the presence of confounding, and did not negatively impact its performance either in the absence of confounding or in the absence of a CDR effect.

span.label: the zero has two causes that produce the same observation - RNA below the threshold of detection, and genuine biological absence - and the paper says the second is CONFLATED WITH the first in the literature's term `extrinsic noise`
span.quote: This is due in part to low starting quantities of RNA such that many genes will be below the threshold of detection, but there is also a biological component to this variation (termed extrinsic noise in the literature) that is conflated with the technical variability

span.label: the cellular detection rate is the fraction of genes detected in a cell, and it REFLECTS BOTH technical factors and biological differences between samples - so the covariate proposed as nuisance is partly the thing being measured
span.quote: We and other groups [ 4 – 7 ] have shown that the proportion of cells with detectable expression reflects both technical factors and biological differences between samples.

span.label: a physical route by which the confounding could arise is named rather than left abstract: TREATED CELLS COULD BECOME LARGER IN VOLUME, which would move the detection rate for the same reason the treatment moves expression
span.quote: It is possible that the CDR and treatment effects could be partially confounded, for example, treated cells could become larger in volume.

span.label: THE NUISANCE VARIABLE IS PARTLY THE SIGNAL. CDR is proposed as `a source of nuisance variation` to adjust for, and the same paper reports that it reflects biological differences too - so the adjustment may remove part of the effect
span.quote: We argue that the cellular detection rate, the fraction of genes expressed in a cell, should be adjusted for as a source of nuisance variation.

span.label: and the size of the problem is stated: THE CDR DEVIANCE ESTIMATES FOR MANY GENES WERE COMPARABLE TO, IF NOT GREATER THAN, THE TREATMENT DEVIANCE ESTIMATES
span.quote: It should also be noted that the CDR deviance estimates for many of the genes were comparable to (if not greater than) the treatment deviance estimates.

span.label: A METHODS PAPER SAYING THE BEST ANSWER TO ITS OWN PROBLEM IS NOT A MODEL: `the OPTIMAL APPROACH to handle confounding between technical and biological effects on the CDR is to DESIGN EXPERIMENTS with biological replicates across multiple batches`
span.quote: the optimal approach to handle confounding between technical and biological effects on the CDR is to design experiments with biological replicates across multiple batches.

span.label: the alternative treatments of CDR each carry an assumption the paper names - centering within treatment groups `would implicitly ASSUME that the observed changes are treatment induced`, and the control-gene offset needs genes ASSUMED to be treatment invariant
span.quote: It is also possible to use CDR as a precision variable (an uncorrelated secondary cause) by centering the CDR within each treatment groups, which makes the CDR measurement orthogonal to treatment. This would implicitly assume that the observed changes are treatment induced, while still modeling the heterogeneity in cell volume within each treatment group.

span.label: the confounding the method's own covariate could cause is SIMULATED and the false positive rate measured with and without CDR control, in the presence and absence of confounding and of a CDR effect
span.note: eliminates: an adjustment that improves fit while destroying the effect it was meant to clean - the four-way comparison is what shows the adjustment does not hurt when there is nothing to adjust for · outcome: held
span.quote: We explored the effect of confounding between the CDR and treatment effects on the MAST false positive rate in the presence and absence of CDR control in the MAST model (Additional file 1 : Figure S4A, B). Controlling for CDR improved the sensitivity and specificity of MAST in the presence of confounding, and did not negatively impact its performance either in the absence of confounding or in the absence of a CDR effect.

span.label: the relative size of the CDR effect against the treatment effect is reported rather than assumed small
span.note: eliminates: a nuisance covariate quietly dominating the model - and the answer is that CDR deviance was COMPARABLE TO OR GREATER THAN treatment deviance for many genes · outcome: failed
span.quote: It should also be noted that the CDR deviance estimates for many of the genes were comparable to (if not greater than) the treatment deviance estimates.

span.label: whether the technical and biological contributions to the detection rate can be separated by any analysis of these data
span.note: eliminates: nothing - the paper states the optimal approach is to design experiments with biological replicates across multiple batches, which is not an analysis · outcome: failed
span.quote: We and other groups [ 4 – 7 ] have shown that the proportion of cells with detectable expression reflects both technical factors and biological differences between samples.

span.label: cellular detection rate - AS USED HERE, IN TWO INCOMPATIBLE ROLES IN ONE PAPER. In the abstract it is `a source of NUISANCE variation` to be adjusted away. In the results it `reflects BOTH technical factors AND biological differences`, its deviance rivals the treatment's, and it may be confounded with treatment because treated cells grow. THE SAME NUMBER IS THE ARTEFACT AND THE SIGNAL
span.quote: We and other groups [ 4 – 7 ] have shown that the proportion of cells with detectable expression reflects both technical factors and biological differences between samples.

span.label: extrinsic noise - the literature's name for the biological half of the variation, and the paper's point is that the NAME DOES NOT SEPARATE IT: it arrives conflated with the technical variability in the same measurement
span.quote: This is due in part to low starting quantities of RNA such that many genes will be below the threshold of detection, but there is also a biological component to this variation (termed extrinsic noise in the literature) that is conflated with the technical variability

span.label: bimodality - AS DEFINED BY THE OBSERVATION, not the cause: expression is `either strongly positive or undetected`. The model parameterises the two modes precisely because it cannot attribute any single zero to one cause or the other
span.quote: First, single-cell expression has repeatedly been shown to exhibit a characteristic bimodal expression pattern, wherein the expression of otherwise abundant genes is either strongly positive or undetected within individual cells.

span.label: critiques → the model of independent expression between genes - `That CDR predicts expression levels CONTRADICTS` it, since an average across many genes could not affect any single gene were expression independent
span.quote: That CDR predicts expression levels contradicts the model of independent expression between genes, because the level of expression (averaged across many genes) would not affect the level in any given gene were expression independent.

span.label: critiques → co-expression analyses that do not adjust for the detection rate, in which `the apparent correlation between genes is greatly inflated`
span.quote: It is especially important to adjust for CDR when testing for co-expression between genes, or the apparent correlation between genes is greatly inflated

span.label: extends → Hicks et al.'s point that confounding between technical and biological effects is best handled by experimental design - conceded here as the optimal approach
span.quote: the optimal approach to handle confounding between technical and biological effects on the CDR is to design experiments with biological replicates across multiple batches.
